(25.1.13) Now this is the Chandoma-daśāha, the milking of the meters; they approach the meters in a forward direction, therefore cattle stand near, facing this way, while consuming.

Now, this is the vow: food indeed is the vow. For nowhere else than in the mouth does food satisfy; since they undertake the vow after [the sacrifice], the means of subsistence through food is thereby placed in the mouth.
Therefore, food that is in the mouth satisfies.
Now, these two Atirātra rites, the Prāyaṇīya and the Udayanīya: by the very same breath with which they set out, they rise again.
(25.2.1) An Atirātra; the twenty-four-fold Prāyaṇīya day; a Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha consisting of four Trivṛt Abhiplava ṣaḍahas;
that constitutes one month. A second [month]; a third; a fourth; a fifth [consisting of] three Trivṛt Abhiplava ṣaḍahas, a Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha, a Trivṛt Bṛhaspatisāman, and three Svarasāmans.

The Divākīrtya day; three Svarasāman days; the Pañcadaśa Indra-stoma Ukthya; the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha beginning with the Trayastriṃśa; one Trivṛt Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha; the ten days of the Dvādaśāha in expanded form (vyūḍha), all Agniṣṭomas with the Trivṛt stoma;
two days consisting of the Udbhid and Balabhid; four Trivṛt Abhiplava Ṣaḍahas; and the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha.
Two six-day periods constitute that month; that is the second, that the third, and that the fourth. There are two *abhiplava* six-day periods, both consisting of the *trivṛt* stoma;

then the *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, the *āyuḥ* day, and the *go* day; then the *chandoma* ten-day period; and finally the twenty-four-fold, the first day, two twenty-eight-fold days, the thirty-fold, the thirty-two-fold, the thirty-six-fold, the forty-fold, the forty-four-fold, and the forty-eight-fold [stomas].

The twenty-four-fold Mahāvrata and the Atirātra are preceded by the Pṛṣṭhya of the Aṅgirases. By means of the Pṛṣṭhya at the beginning, the Aṅgirases ascended to the heavenly world; therefore, when they employ the Pṛṣṭhya stotras at the beginning, it is for the sake of ascending to the heavenly world. The Pṛṣṭhya stotras are indeed food; thus food is placed at the very front. Therefore, food situated in the mouth satisfies. The Pṛṣṭhya stotras are cattle; they thus find firm support in cattle.

(25.2.4) Whatever else there is besides the two *cakras* and the *sākavṛd*s is the same as [the pattern] up to the *chandoma* days of the ten-day period. (25.2.5) Now, this *chandoma* ten-day period is the milking of the meters; they proceed with the higher meters for the sake of non-degeneration.
This indeed is the path leading to the gods; those who undertake this reach the path leading to the gods. Now, this is the vow.
(PB 25.2.6) Now, these two *atirātra*s, the *prāyaṇīya* and the *udayanīya*: by means of that very breath through which they set out, they rise up again.

(PB 25.3.1) There is an *atirātra*; [then] a month with the *trivṛt*, a month with the *pañcadaśa*, a month with the *saptadaśa*, a month with the *ekaviṃśa*, a month with the *triṇava*, a month with the *trayastriṃśa*, a month with the *mahāvrata*, a month with the *trayastriṃśa*, and [a month] with the *triṇava*.
A month with twenty-one-fold [stomas], a month with seventeen-fold, a month with fifteen-fold, a month with nine-fold, and an Atirātra.

The seasons did not find firm standing; they found firm standing by means of this [rite]. Those who desire a firm foundation should perform it; they indeed find firm standing. There are six seasons; verily, by this they find firm standing in the seasons.
In that they employ [the stomas] in the middle when it has proceeded, food is thereby placed in the middle; therefore, he nourishes in the middle.
This sacrificial session (*sattrāyaṇa*) is indeed like a bird; whatever desire they desire, they attain by means of it, for wherever a bird desires, it attains that very thing.

They proceed with the *trivṛt* stoma and they emerge with the *trivṛt*; the *trivṛt* is indeed the breath among the *stomas*. Thus, they proceed by means of the breaths and they find firm support in the breaths. Dṛti and Vātavant were both disciples of Khāṇḍava. At the Viṣuvat day, Vātavant rose [to perform the rite] and completed it; Dṛti, however, remained behind. Therefore, there are fewer descendants of Vātavant and more descendants of Dṛti.
(Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 25.4.1) They remain consecrated for a month; at the end of that month they purchase the Soma. For them there are twelve Upasad days;

having performed the Upasad rites and having bound the Soma, they offer the Agnihotra for a month, they sacrifice with the New and Full Moon sacrifices for a month, with the Vaiśvadeva for a month, with the Varuṇapraghāsas for a month, with the Sākamedhas for a month, and with the Śunāsīrya sacrifice accompanied by the Trivṛt Stoma for a month.

A month with the fifteen-fold [stoma], a month with the seventeen-fold, a month with the twenty-one-fold, a month with the twenty-seven-fold; eighteen days of the thirty-three-fold, ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra;
the Agnihotra, the Daśahotṛ, the New and Full Moon sacrifices, the Caturhotṛ, the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, the Pañcahotṛ, and the Soma sacrifice, the Saptahotṛ.

(25.4.3) Indeed, those who undertake this [rite] sacrifice with the entire sacrifice; they become everything. (25.4.4) They are all drinkers from the *kuṇḍa* vessels; they consume [the soma] from cups without handles (*atsaruka*).
(25.4.5) He who is the *hotṛ* is the *adhvaryu*, he is the *potṛ*; he who is the *udgātṛ* is the *neṣṭṛ*, he is the *acchāvāka*; he who is the *maitrāvaruṇa* [is the same].
He who is the Prastotṛ is the Brahman; he who is the Pratiprasthātṛ is the Pratihartṛ; he who is the Agnīdh is the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; he who is the Unnetṛ is the Grāvastut.
The Gṛhapati is the Subrahmaṇya, and the Subrahmaṇya is the Gṛhapati.
They remain consecrated for a year; they perform the Upasad rites for a year; the Soma-pressing lasts for a year.

(25.5.2) For one year they remain consecrated; by that they perform austerity. In that they perform the *upasad* rites for a year, they purify themselves by that. In that the Soma is pressed for a year, they go to the world of the gods by that. (25.5.3) By this very means, the gods, having accumulated austerity, attained all prosperity; those who undertake this attain all prosperity.

(25.6.1) There are three years of the *trivṛt* type, three of the *pañcadaśa* type, three of the *saptadaśa* type, and three of the *ekaviṃśa* type; [this constitutes] Prajāpati’s twelve-year [cycle].

(25.6.2) By means of this, indeed, Prajāpati attained the procreation of all; those who undertake this attain the procreation of all. (25.6.3) In that there are three years of the *trivṛt* type, the *trivṛt* is splendor and spiritual luster (*brāhmavarcasa*); it is splendor.

Thus they obtain spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). In that there are three fifteen-versed stomas, and the fifteen is strength and vigor, they obtain strength and vigor itself. In that there are three seventeen-versed stomas, and the seventeen is indeed food, they obtain the eating of food itself.
In that there are three twenty-one-versed stomas, and the twenty-one is a firm foundation, they find a firm foundation at the very end of the sacrifice.
(25.6.4) By means of this, indeed, the Naimiśīyas attained all prosperity; they who undertake this attain all prosperity.

(25.6.5) They rose up from among those of the seventeen-fold [stoma], and they said: "Whosoever among us shall prosper in offspring, let him complete this sacrificial session. Desiring that very thing, the Brahmins sit for the sacrificial session.
Nine years of the *trivṛt* [stoma], nine of the *pañcadaśa*, nine of the *saptadaśa*, and nine of the *ekaviṃśa*: this is the thirty-six-year sacrificial session of the Śāktyas.

By means of this, Gaurīviti Śākta, through the *tarasapuroḍāśa* at Yavyāvatī, attained all prosperity; indeed, those who undertake this attain all prosperity. This sacrificial session is the *bṛhatī*; the *bṛhatī* is the self-sovereignty (*svārājya*) among the meters. Those who undertake this attain self-sovereignty.
This is the Daśavīra of the Śāktyas; ten heroes are born to those who undertake this.
There are twenty-five Trivṛt years, twenty-five Pañcadaśa years, twenty-five Saptadaśa years, and twenty-five Ekaviṃśa years: this is the hundred-year sacrifice of the Sādhyas.
The Sādhyas, indeed, were gods who existed before the [other] gods; they undertook this sacrificial session.

By that they prospered; together with their cattle and their men, they all went indeed to the heavenly world. "In this very way, those who undertake this go together to the heavenly world" (PB 25.8.3).

This sacrificial session (*sattra*) is indeed life; man has a lifespan of a hundred years. As much as there is of life, that they obtain, for there is no sacrificial session that exceeds the span of life.

Regarding this, it was said: "Those were many days in former times, before the rising of the sun, from which the Dawn appeared like a lover coming toward her, as if she were not going away again" (PB 25.8.5).
By means of the course of the Jyotiṣṭoma, they go; they indeed become light.

The twenty-one-fold chant is at the end of the *stomas*; the twenty-one-fold is indeed the foundation at the end of the *stomas*. By means of the twenty-one-fold, they find firm support at the very end of the sacrifice.

(PB 25.8.6) It is an *atirātra*, a thousand days, and an *atirātra*: this is Agni’s attainment of a thousandfold success. (PB 25.9.1–2) By means of this, Agni attained the impulse of all; those who undertake this attain the impulse of all.

(25.9.3) Indeed, everything is edible for Agni; everything becomes edible for those who undertake this rite. (25.9.4) Now, as to why it is the "thousand-obtaining" (*sahasrasāvya*): the supreme *virāj* consists of a thousand syllables; they find firm support in that very supreme *virāj*.
(25.10.1) They undergo initiation at the place where the Sarasvatī disappears.

For them there are twelve initiation days (*dīkṣā*) and twelve *upasads*. On the day that the *atirātra* sacrifice takes place, they drive away the calves; when the *atirātra* has been completed, they sacrifice with the *sānnāyya* (milk offering).

Having sacrificed with the *sānnāyya*, the *adhvaryu* throws a wooden pin (*śamyā*); where it falls, that is the *gārhapatya* fire. From there he strides thirty-six steps forward; that is the *āhavanīya* fire.

The *sadas* is wheel-shaped; the *havirdhāna* shed is wheel-shaped; the *āgnīdhra* shed is wheel-shaped; the sacrificial post has its base in a mortar. Having drawn [the earth] out, they merely strew it; they do not dig the *uparava* pits.
They proceed toward that [moon] while it is waxing during the new-moon night. On the full-moon day, for them, there is the *goṣṭoma-stoma*, an *ukthya* sacrifice with the *bṛhat-sāman*.

When the Goṣṭoma has been completed, they perform the Full-moon sacrifice; they proceed by means of the Full-moon sacrifice as that [sacrifice] wanes. For them, on the new moon day, there is the Āyuṣṭoma-stoma, an Ukthya, which is the "Course of Mitra and Varuṇa.
By this very [rite], Mitra and Varuṇa indeed conquered these worlds; Mitra and Varuṇa are indeed day and night.
Day is Mitra, night is Varuṇa; indeed, Mitra and Varuṇa are the two halves of the month. That which waxes is Mitra, that which wanes is Varuṇa. This very Mitra sheds seed into Varuṇa.
By means of Sarasvatī, the gods supported the Āditya; she did not hold him steady, and she collapsed.
Therefore, just as Kubjimatī supported him with the Bṛhatī, she extended [the sacrifice]; therefore the Bṛhatī is the most powerful of the meters, for with it they supported the sun.
They proceed against the current, for they do not follow the current; indeed, they go eight times by the front wing, for each one returns toward that.
At the Dṛṣadvatī itself (PB 25.10.15), having offered a *caru* oblation to Apām Napāt at the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī, they then proceed (PB 25.10.16).

There are forty-four *āśvīna* stages from the disappearance of the Sarasvatī to the Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa; that far from here is the heavenly world. By a path commensurate with the Sarasvatī, one reaches the heavenly world.
By means of this, Namī Sāpya, the king of Videha, went straight to the heavenly world; "he went straight" (*añjasāgāt*), and that is why they are called the *Añjaskīyas*.
He entered this purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*): that pool which is to the north of the Sthūlārma. Then a hundred cows of his became a thousand.
Among those hundred cows, they drive forth a bull.
When they reach a thousand, then there is the rising;
when they suffer total loss, then there is the rising; when the householder dies, then there is the rising;
when they come to the Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa, then there is the rising.

(22) Having gone to Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa, they perform a sacrifice to Agni Kāma; in that sacrifice, having given a mare and a human female as two milch-cows, (23) they descend into the Yamunā for the ritual bath at Kārapacava.
(1) It is an Atirātra with the Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa stomas; it is the Ayana of Indra and Agni, the Go and Āyus sacrifices, and the Indrakukṣi Atirātra.
(25.11.2) By means of this, indeed, Indra and Agni surpassed all other deities; those who undertake this [rite] surpass all other offspring.
(25.11.3) Indra and Agni are the most powerful among the gods; those who undertake this become the most powerful.

(25.11.4) Now, as for the fact that the threefold and the fifteenfold [stomas] are the course of Indra and Agni, and the Go and Āyus [sāmans] are the two bellies of Indra, it is for the sake of non-disturbance.
(25.12.1) An Atirātra, the Jyotis, the Gauḥ, and the Āyus—this three-day rite, the Viśvajit and the Abhijit as the two "bellies of Indra," and an Atirātra.
(25.12.2) By means of this, Vārya conquered this world.
(25.12.3) When they say, "The path of Aryaman," this indeed is the path traveled by the gods.
(25.12.4) Those who undertake this reach the path that leads to the gods. (25.12.5) Therefore, this [sun] appears as if most ruddy from the sky, for the path is indeed most ruddy.

(25.12.6) Now, as for the fact that the Jyotis, Gaur, and Āyus [days], the three-day period, the Viśvajit, and the Abhijit—these two being the "bellies of Indra"—are included, it is for the sake of non-disturbance.
(25.13.1) For one year he should tend the cows of a Brāhmaṇa; for one year he should kindle his fires on the barren Naitandhava soil; after a year, having covered them, he should establish his fires.
(25.13.2) On the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī, he should go as far as a yoke-pin’s throw with an offering on eight potsherds to Agni.
(25.13.3) Indra and Ruśama cast a die; whichever of us first goes around the earth, that one [shall win].

Indra went around Kurukṣetra, thinking, "I shall conquer the earth. Ruśama said to him, "I have conquered you. Indra replied, "I alone have conquered you. The two of them asked the gods; those gods said, "The altar of Prajāpati is indeed as large as Kurukṣetra. Thus, the two of them did not conquer one another.

(25.13.4) He who, with an offering on eight potsherds for Agni, goes along the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī as far as the Śamyā-throw, and reaches the Yamunā at the Triplakṣa [confluence] for the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), truly becomes hidden from men.
(25.14.1) [The offerings are]: a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra, and a pap (caru) for the Viśve Devas.

(25.14.2) One who has not been initiated puts on a black antelope skin. In that he, being uninitiated, puts on the black antelope skin, he thereby attains whatever human prosperity there is. (25.14.3) Then, in that he performs austerity, he thereby attains whatever divine [prosperity] there is.
(25.14.4) In that there is a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, the deities indeed have Agni as their mouth; thus, from the very beginning, he reaches the deities.

He prospers; moreover, he thereby obtains the morning pressing. Now, as for the fact that there is a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra—since the midday pressing belongs to Indra—he thereby obtains the midday pressing. And as for the fact that there is a pap for the Viśve Devas—since the third pressing belongs to the Viśve Devas—he thereby obtains the third pressing.
By this, indeed, the divine sage Puroḍa attained all prosperity; he who undertakes this attains all prosperity.

There are two *atirātra* sacrifices on both sides and an *agniṣṭoma* in the middle; thus the year is entirely composed of tens. The *viṣuvant* day is the twelfth, and the *sarpasāman* chants are performed on the *viṣuvant*. By this, indeed, the serpents established themselves in these worlds; those who undertake this establish themselves in these worlds.

Jarvara was the *gṛhapati*; Dhṛtarāṣṭra Airāvata was the *brahman*; Pṛthuśravas Daureśravasa was the *udgātṛ*; Glāva and Ajagāva were the *prastotṛ* and *pratihartṛ*; Datta Tāpasa was the *hotṛ*; Śitipṛṣṭha was the *maitrāvaruṇa*;
Takṣaka Vaiśāleya was the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*; Śikha and Anuśikha were the *neṣṭṛ* and *potṛ*; Aruṇa Āṭa was the *acchāvāka*; and Timirgha was the *grāvaṣṭut*.

Dāureśruta was the Āgnīdhra; Kautastau were the two Adhvaryus, namely Arimejaya and Janamejaya; Arbuda was the Grāvastut; Dajira was the Subrahmaṇya; Cakka and Piśaṅga were the two Unnetṛs; and Ṣaṇḍa and Kuṣaṇḍa were the Abhigara and Apagara.
By means of this [rite], the serpents conquered death; they who perform this conquer death.

"Therefore, having cast off their worn-out skin, those serpents slither away, for they have conquered death. The serpents are indeed the Ādityas; thus, the splendor of these who perform this [rite] becomes like that of the Ādityas" (PB 25.16.1).
The first year is the *Gavām Ayana* (Course of the Cows), then that of the Ādityas, and then that of the Aṅgirases.

By means of this, indeed, the cattle attained progeny and abundance; they who perform this rite are procreated and become numerous. By means of this, indeed, the Ādityas established themselves in these worlds; they who perform this rite establish themselves [in these worlds].
By means of this, indeed, the Aṅgirases went to the heavenly world; they who perform this rite go to the heavenly world.
(25.16.3) Para Āṣṭhāra, Trasadasyu Paurukutsa, Vītahavya Śrāyasa, and Kakṣīvat Auśija—these, desiring offspring, undertook this sacrificial session (*sattra*). They produced a thousand sons each;
indeed, those who undertake this likewise produce a thousand sons each.
(25.17.1) An Atirātra, a thousand threefold-stoma years, and an Atirātra—this is Prajāpati’s thousand-year sacrifice.
(25.17.2) By means of this, indeed, Prajāpati attained the procreation of all; those who undertake this attain the procreation of all.
(25.17.3) This, indeed, was what Prajāpati, when he was worn out and deluded, undertook; by it he drove away old age. Those who undertake this strike away old age.
This is the thousand-year sacrifice of Prajāpati. By means of this, Prajāpati indeed attained all prosperity; they who undertake this attain all prosperity.
There are fifty-five threefold years, fifty-five fifteenfold years, fifty-five seventeenfold years, and fifty-five twenty-one-fold years of the Viśvasṛjs.
By means of this, the Viśvasṛjs indeed created this universe; because they created the universe, they are called the Viśvasṛjs.
Everything is born after them who enter upon this.
Tapas is the householder; Brahman is the Brahman-priest; the wife is the immortal; the Udgātṛ is the past;
the Prastotṛ is the future; the seasons are the Upagātṛs; the seasonal periods are the Sadasyas; Truth is the Hotṛ; the Maitrāvaruṇa is the sacrifice; the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is vigor.
Radiance and honor are the Neṣṭṛ and Potṛ; glory is the Acchāvāka; Agni himself is the Āgnīdhra; fortune is the Grāvastut; vigor is the Unnetṛ;
speech is the Subrahmaṇya; breath is the Adhvaryu; out-breath is the Pratiprasthātṛ; direction is the Viśāstṛ; strength is the Dhruvagopa;
the quarters are the Haviṣpēṣyās; day and night are the two Idhmavāhas; and death is the Śamitṛ—these undergo consecration.

Regarding this, there is this verse: "The creators of the universe sat for their first sacrificial session for a thousand years, proceeding with the *prasuta* offering. They were the guardians of the world, golden birds named Brahman.

Those who undertake this [session] attain the same world (*salokatā*), the same power (*sārṣṭitā*), and union (*sāyujya*) with Brahman. This is the thousand-year session of the creators of the universe; by means of it, the creators of the universe indeed attained all prosperity, all prosperity.
They attain supernatural power who approach this.
